The kittens were initially spotted roaming the subway before disappearing temporarily, leading to police deployment for crowd control as trains remained stopped. After reappearing, the animals were safely transported to a Brooklyn animal foster home. Subway operations resumed shortly after the incident resolved.

article_content: India’s securities regulator SEBI has approved a groundbreaking framework allowing partial ownership of real estate assets, aiming to make property investments more accessible. While progressing this reform, the regulator chose to delay proposed changes to delisting processes due to limited historical data on recent delistings. SEBI Chair Madhabi Puri Buch stated the board wants more stakeholder consultations before finalizing delisting rules. The new system introduces small/medium REITs requiring ₹50 crore in assets (vs ₹500 crore for standard REITs), enabling investors to pool funds via SPVs for property purchases. Investors will gain exposure to pre-leased properties offering rental income and potential appreciation. SEBI is also fast-tracking same-day trade settlements (T+0) after industry feedback recommended bypassing intermediate steps to reduce costs. Regulatory updates include enhanced oversight of major indices amid growing passive investment trends, with SEBI shifting focus from regulating all indices to prioritizing significant ones.

A kikapcsolódási szabályok módosítását megakasztva figyelembe vette a korai adatok korlátozottságát. article_content: WASHINGTON — Pro-Palestinian demonstrations erupted globally on Saturday, with tens of thousands rallying in cities like Washington, Milan, and Paris to demand an end to Israel’s bombardment of Gaza. The protests underscored deepening international concern over the escalating civilian toll in the Israel-Hamas war. Participants in nations with significant Muslim populations—including the U.S., U.K., and France—voiced frustration with their governments’ support for Israel amid intensified strikes on hospitals and residential areas. According to Gaza’s Hamas-run health authority, Palestinian fatalities have surpassed 9,448, while Israel reports over 1,400 deaths, primarily from Hamas’ Oct. 7 attack that ignited the conflict. In Washington, crowds draped in black-and-white keffiyehs chanted 'Palestine will be free!' near the White House, displaying signs accusing President Biden of complicity. Protesters laid out dozens of small white body bags symbolizing child casualties and demanded an immediate ceasefire. Some demonstrators, like Renad Dayem from Cleveland, criticized Biden’s alignment with Israel’s policies, stating they seek leaders who reject 'puppetry' to foreign governments. Meanwhile, 27-year-old Jinane Ennasri of New York expressed disillusionment with Biden’s stance, vowing to abstain from the 2024 election unless policies shift. Biden, vacationing in Delaware, briefly acknowledged U.S. efforts to secure a humanitarian pause but offered no new commitments. Jewish protester Steve Strauss condemned Israel’s tactics, asserting, 'They’re killing as many Palestinians as possible.' In Paris, thousands braved rain to chant 'Stop the massacre,' while authorities warned against antisemitic rhetoric. Concurrently, France faced a stabbing incident targeting a Jewish woman in Lyon, marked by a swastika on her door. London saw 11 arrests at a protest, including a terrorism charge for inciting hatred via signage. Berlin deployed 1,000 officers after prior violent clashes, banning antisemitic or pro-violence statements. Across Europe, demonstrations highlighted both solidarity with Gaza and fears of rising extremism, with Yara Abushab—a Gazan medical student in Italy—describing her homeland’s devastation as 'indescribable.'

article_content: Amateur football team Box Sash FC sparked curiosity after winning their local Wimbledon & District Saturday League Division Three title. The squad celebrated with a five-mile open-top bus parade through south-west London, featuring custom banners, balloons, and champagne toasts. Despite lacking a large fanbase, the 30-strong team drew amused crowds during their circuit of Wimbledon, starting and ending at the Rose and Crown pub. Formed in August 2022, the group—primarily ex-Leeds University students—secured promotion to Division Two after winning 13 of 16 matches and scoring 61 goals. Captain Matt Cook described the parade as 'a bit of a laugh' that still raised £250 for the Generations Foundation, supporting vulnerable children in Merton. Goalkeeper Patrick Ellis highlighted the season's blend of success and fun, vowing to challenge for titles again next year.

article_content: Parents navigate a delicate balance between documenting their children's milestones and managing social media perceptions. A Tinybeans study finds half of Australian parents worry about annoying friends through excessive baby photo sharing, despite 75% fearing online safety risks. This anxiety arises amid reports of Instagram's 'baby role-playing' trend, where stolen images fuel fictional narratives under hashtags like #babyrp. Launched in 2012 by founders Sarah-Jane Kurtini, Stephen O'Young, and Eddie Geller, Tinybeans provides a private platform for 500,000+ users to securely share developmental milestones. Bondi Beach mother Lee Bradford illustrates this challenge: capturing 100-150 photos daily of her daughter Isla led to friend unfollows until she migrated to Tinybeans' controlled environment. 'Tinybeans lets parents celebrate parenthood without risking social backlash,' says Kurtini, emphasizing the platform's focus on child safety and familial connection.

article_content: Jon Hamm has been named host of the 2013 ESPYS, airing live July 17 at 9 PM ET from the Nokia Theatre in Los Angeles on ESPN. Executive producer Maura Mandt highlighted Hamm's comedic timing and sports enthusiasm, referencing his work on '30 Rock' and Saturday Night Live. Previous hosts include Justin Timberlake and Seth Meyers. Hamm joked about balancing athletics and hosting: 'I need to decide which cleats go best with a tuxedo.' The Arthur Ashe Courage Award will honor Good Morning America's Robin Roberts, who returned to work after a six-month bone marrow transplant recovery period.
